visual: Architectural evergreen with long, narrow, sword-shaped leaves in rich burgundy-red to deep bronze-purple. Forms a fountain-like rosette, eventually developing a woody trunk. Mature plants may produce fragrant creamy-white flowers in summer.
water: Water regularly while establishing and during prolonged dry spells. Allow the soil surface to dry slightly between waterings. Established plants tolerate moderate drought. Avoid waterlogging, especially in winter.
aspect: Full sun to partial shade. Best in a warm, sheltered position with protection from cold, drying winds. Light shade can help prevent foliage scorching.
soil: Fertile, well-drained loam, sand, chalk or improved clay. Tolerates acidic, neutral and alkaline soils.
soilWarning: Avoid heavy, persistently wet soil and cold winter waterlogging. Improve drainage in clay soils and protect container roots from freezing.
prune: Minimal pruning required. Remove dead or damaged lower leaves as needed. Remove frost-damaged growth in spring once new shoots appear.
toxicity: Potentially toxic to cats and dogs if ingested, causing digestive upset. Avoid allowing pets to chew foliage.
hardinessNote: H3 · −5 to 1°C. Hardy outdoors in mild coastal and sheltered UK gardens. Protect from prolonged frost and cold winter winds. Young and container-grown plants are particularly vulnerable.
resilience: Moderately drought tolerant once established, with good wind and coastal tolerance in mild climates. Vulnerable to prolonged hard frost and winter wet. Occasional scale insects, red spider mites and cordyline slime flux.
uses: Architectural focal point, tropical-style borders, coastal gardens, Mediterranean planting, patio containers and contemporary landscapes.
